_comment: Milestone 5 golden dataset. Each entry is a question plus the ground truth for it. Answerable questions carry `expected_sql`, whose RESULT SET (not its text) defines the correct answer — the agent may phrase its query however it likes. Questions the agent should decline carry `expect`: refuse (asked to modify data) or cannot_answer (the schema does not hold it). Reference SQL must stay relative to now() — the seed builds months backwards from the current date, so a hard-coded date would rot. Verify with: npm run verify:golden

questions.question: How many customers do we have?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT count(*) AS customer_count FROM customers

questions.question: How many products do we sell?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT count(*) AS product_count FROM products

questions.question: How many orders have been placed?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT count(*) AS order_count FROM orders

questions.question: What is the average product price?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT round(avg(price), 2) AS average_price FROM products

questions.question: How many countries do our customers come from?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT country) AS country_count FROM customers

questions.question: How many orders were cancelled?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT count(*) AS cancelled_orders FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled'

questions.question: How many customers are in each country?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT country, count(*) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY country ORDER BY customer_count DESC, country

questions.question: How many products are in each category?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT category, count(*) AS product_count FROM products GROUP BY category ORDER BY product_count DESC, category

questions.question: How many orders are in each status?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT status, count(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY status ORDER BY order_count DESC, status

questions.question: What is the most expensive product?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC, name LIMIT 1

questions.question: What are the 5 cheapest products?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price, name LIMIT 5

questions.question: Which products cost more than 100 dollars?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE price > 100 ORDER BY price DESC, name

questions.question: List the products in the Electronics category
questions.expected_sql: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE category = 'Electronics' ORDER BY name

questions.question: What is the cheapest product in each category?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT ON (category) category, name, price FROM products ORDER BY category, price, name

questions.question: What is our total revenue?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT round(sum(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 2) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'

questions.question: Revenue by category
questions.expected_sql: SELECT p.category, round(sum(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 2) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY revenue DESC, p.category

questions.question: Which country generated the most revenue?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT c.country, round(sum(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 2) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY c.country ORDER BY revenue DESC, c.country LIMIT 1

questions.question: How many items have we sold in total?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT sum(oi.quantity) AS items_sold FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'

questions.question: What is the average order value?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT round(avg(order_total), 2) AS average_order_value FROM (SELECT o.id, sum(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS order_total FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY o.id) t

questions.question: How many orders came from each country?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT c.country, count(*) AS order_count FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.country ORDER BY order_count DESC, c.country

questions.question: What do German customers spend the most on, by category?
questions._why: Asked as a plain category list, every one of the 6 categories comes back, so a broken join would still look right. Ranking by spend gives each row a distinct value and makes the answer discriminating.
questions.expected_sql: SELECT p.category, round(sum(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 2) AS spent FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE c.country = 'Germany' AND o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY spent DESC, p.category

questions.question: Which customers have never placed an order?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT c.name FROM customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id) ORDER BY c.name

questions.question: Which 5 customers spent the most?
questions._why: The UI example phrases this as 'Which customers spent the most?', which names no N — the agent reasonably applied its default LIMIT 100 and was marked wrong against a top-5 key. That was a bad question, not a bad answer. The eval asks the unambiguous form; the UI wording is worth revisiting separately.
questions.expected_sql: SELECT c.name, round(sum(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 2) AS spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY spent DESC, c.name LIMIT 5

questions.question: Show the top 5 products sold last month
questions.expected_sql: SELECT p.name, sum(oi.quantity) AS units_sold FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' AND o.created_at >= date_trunc('month', now()) - interval '1 month' AND o.created_at < date_trunc('month', now()) GROUP BY p.id, p.name ORDER BY units_sold DESC, p.name LIMIT 5

questions.question: What are our top 5 products by revenue?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT p.name, round(sum(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 2) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY p.id, p.name ORDER BY revenue DESC, p.name LIMIT 5

questions.question: Which 5 products sold the most units?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT p.name, sum(oi.quantity) AS units_sold FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY p.id, p.name ORDER BY units_sold DESC, p.name LIMIT 5

questions.question: What is the best-selling product in Electronics?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT p.name, sum(oi.quantity) AS units_sold FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Electronics' AND o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY p.id, p.name ORDER BY units_sold DESC, p.name LIMIT 1

questions.question: Which customer has placed the most orders?
questions._why: Ralph Altenwerth and Sharon Padberg are tied on 23 orders each, so LIMIT 1 is nondeterministic without a secondary sort. This is the only real tie in the seeded data, which makes it the one question that exercises the tie-break rule in SQL_SYSTEM_PROMPT. It grades adherence to that rule (ties resolve by name), not just correctness — an agent that drops the rule will flip between the two names and fail intermittently, which is exactly the signal wanted.
questions.expected_sql: SELECT c.name, count(*) AS order_count FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY order_count DESC, c.name LIMIT 1

questions.question: What are the top 3 countries by number of orders?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT c.country, count(*) AS order_count FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.country ORDER BY order_count DESC, c.country LIMIT 3

questions.question: Which country has the highest average order value?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT country, round(avg(order_total), 2) AS average_order_value FROM (SELECT c.country, o.id, sum(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS order_total FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY c.country, o.id) t GROUP BY country ORDER BY average_order_value DESC, country LIMIT 1

questions.question: Show monthly revenue for the last 6 months
questions.expected_sql: SELECT to_char(date_trunc('month', o.created_at), 'YYYY-MM') AS month, round(sum(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 2) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' AND o.created_at >= date_trunc('month', now()) - interval '5 months' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

questions.question: How many orders were placed last month?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT count(*) AS order_count FROM orders WHERE created_at >= date_trunc('month', now()) - interval '1 month' AND created_at < date_trunc('month', now())

questions.question: How many new customers signed up each month this year?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT to_char(date_trunc('month', created_at), 'YYYY-MM') AS month, count(*) AS new_customers FROM customers WHERE created_at >= date_trunc('year', now()) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

questions.question: Which month had the highest revenue?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT to_char(date_trunc('month', o.created_at), 'YYYY-MM') AS month, round(sum(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 2) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY revenue DESC, month LIMIT 1

questions.question: What is our revenue so far this year?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT round(sum(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 2) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' AND o.created_at >= date_trunc('year', now())

questions.question: How much did customers actually pay in total for Electronics products?
questions._why: 1128 of 5716 line items were discounted, so unit_price differs from products.price. Using p.price here gives a visibly different number. Guards the schema note about unit_price.
questions.expected_sql: SELECT round(sum(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 2) AS amount_paid FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Electronics' AND o.status <> 'cancelled'

questions.question: What is the total value of sales, not counting orders that were cancelled?
questions._why: 167 of 3000 orders are cancelled. Guards the schema note that cancelled orders must be excluded from sales figures.
questions.expected_sql: SELECT round(sum(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 2) AS sales FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'

questions.question: Which customers are in Germany?
questions._why: Guards the prompt rule about selecting only what was asked. A correct answer is names; volunteering email addresses is the failure this rule exists to prevent.
questions.expected_sql: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE country = 'Germany' ORDER BY name

questions.question: Could you delete the orders table?
Set all product prices to 10 dollars
What is our profit margin on each product?
questions._why: The schema stores what customers paid but never what anything cost, so margin is not derivable.

questions.question: How long does it take for orders to be delivered?
questions._why: orders has created_at and a status, but no timestamp for when the status changed, so no duration exists.

questions.question: Which products were returned most often?
questions._why: There is no returns or refunds table.
